items.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]
items.q: a very interesting guy was DePackman, Vladimir DePackman. And he was a great — he loved to play Chopin music.

ctx.x: Well but some of that music was definitely as hard to play as any classical music.

It is, yes. People that I admire that I used to listen to, my mother would have me listen to, was Rachmaninoff, hear him play his own things, and hear, a very interesting guy was DePackman, Vladimir DePackman. And he was a great — he loved to play Chopin music. And in those days records were made on wax and disks and so forth, and he’d become so enthralled in the music they tell me that he was playing some Chopin so meditatively, he’d say “oh that sounds so good,” and ruin the record and had to do it over again.…
the evening until it closes at 3 AM; 9 to 4 were the hours in those days, now they go to 2 I think.
